summary: Jeff Shore is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served at Hanazono University as a professor from circa 1992 to 2018 and was named professor emeritus there circa 2018.
Jeff Watt works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under teacher Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.

Jeff Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, mentored by Taitetsu Unno (attested 2009) and postdoctoral mentor Myōsei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long is an indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. He earned a BA at Notre Dame (~1987-1991), followed by an MA (~1991-1993) and PhD (~1993-2000) at Chicago, before joining Elizabethtown College in 2000.

Jeffrey Broughton specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University in 1975 and served as a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University (attested 2004).

Jeffrey Clark Ruff is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Missouri State and UC Santa Barbara (PhD 2002 under David Gordon White). After holding teaching and director roles, he became Assistant Professor at Marshall University in 2002.

Jeffrey Davis Schoening is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Washington (attested 1991), where he studied under advisor Sanghasen Singh and doctoral supervisor Collett Cox.

Jeffrey Hopkins (1940-2024) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated under Geshe Wangyal, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Kelden, he completed his PhD at Wisconsin-Madison (~1968-1972) and was a professor at the University of Virginia (1973-2005).

Jeffrey J. Kripal specializes in religious studies and Indology. After studying at Conception Seminary College and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1987-1993), he became the J. Newton Rayzor Chair at Rice University circa 2002 and founded Rice University in 2014.

Jeffrey Kotyk specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA at Komazawa University (2015-2016) and a PhD at Leiden University (2017) under James A. Benn, later holding posts at McMaster University and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman is an academic who held posts at Cornell, Yale, Johns Hopkins (~1974-1983), and Boston University (~1995). He has also served visiting professorships at Harvard, UC Berkeley, CUNY Graduate Center, Washington University in St. Louis, and MIT.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson is an Indologist who earned his BA and PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty posts at the University of Toronto (1969-1980) and UC Berkeley (1981-1992), among other appointments.

Jeffrey Newmark is a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. He completed studies at Harvard University in 1996 and the University of British Columbia in 2009, and he held an appointment at the University of Winnipeg.

Jeffrey S. Lidke is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He has held academic posts at Berry College and served as a visiting assistant professor of religion at the University of Virginia (attested 2003).

Jeffrey Samuels is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia (attested 2002) under Karen C. Lang, and he became Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Western Kentucky University (attested 2013).

Jeffrey Stout is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. After completing studies at Brown University (~1968-1972) and a PhD at Princeton University (~1972-1976), he served as a professor at Princeton University from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from UNC Wilmington, the University of Tennessee, and UCLA (PhD attested 2013 under Gregory Schopen). He has held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego (attested 2013).

Jenkuan Shih is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi, having previously studied under MA supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

Jennifer Jung-Kim specializes in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Her career includes posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, where she served as assistant director (attested 2016) and lecturer (attested 2026).

Jens Braarvig is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. In 2003, he held professor positions at the University of Oslo and the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology (circa 2003).
